clue.text: Settee Moir abused in bits of Shooting Stars?

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Moir has trashed a settee during a comedy show called Shooting Stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooting Stars was a British TV comedy panel show, which steers you away from the night sky; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting stars are meteors, and the fragments of them that reach the ground are rocks of this kind.

clue.text: Use up a bit of energy doing no good around north Ohio

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter
around says one phrase wraps itself about the letter that follows

blocks.note: first letter of energy
someone 'at it' is up to mischief
N is the abbreviation for north
O is a postal-style abbreviation for Ohio

explanation.surface: An American in Ohio grumbles about wasting energy on pointless activity.
explanation.walkthrough: AT IT goes around N, then E goes in front and O at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings or time is to consume or deplete part of them, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Demand Congress must release last of files

indicators.note: releasing a letter lets it go, so it drops out of the word
the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: congress in the sense of sexual intercourse
final letter of files

explanation.surface: Congress is pressed to make some documents public on demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature, but it means sexual intercourse; drop its S to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a payment or promise is to insist on it and obtain it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Singer on drug taking break in squalid room

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the first goes first
taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: a singer is an informer who 'sings' to the police, a rat
HOL is short for holiday
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A vocalist high on drugs takes a rest in a grubby room.
explanation.walkthrough: A singer is underworld slang for an informer, someone who sings to the police; the drug is the usual crossword ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rathole is slang for a filthy, cramped dwelling fit only for rodents.

clue.text: Facial hair of jazz fan sent up by the Man

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: The boss mocks a jazz lover's moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: TACHE is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: A tache is short for moustache, the hair grown on the upper lip.

clue.text: Pin hoax on model-type and the French

blocks.note: a skit is a send-up or spoof
the Model T Ford
French for the

explanation.surface: Someone pins the blame for a hoax on a fashion model and the French.
explanation.definitionFit: In ninepins or skittles, each wooden target knocked down is called a pin.

clue.text: Stalk 9 criminals with police backing

indicators.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 9 across, which asks for the final letter of the next word
backing means going in reverse, so the word reads from right to left

blocks.note: final letter of criminals
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Police help a gang of nine criminals to stalk someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is AT LAST, so '9 criminals' reads 'at last criminals', its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem is the main stalk of a plant, the part bearing leaves and flowers.

clue.text: As dope cut fantastically might become thus?

definitions.text: As dope cut fantastically might become thus?

indicators.note: done fantastically means done wildly and imaginatively, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Smoking heavily adulterated cannabis might leave you in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a user of cut dope might end up like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced out describes being dazed or disoriented, the state drugs commonly produce.

clue.text: Bachelor in Barking hears Aussie's gas constantly

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go haywire

blocks.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single man in the London district of Barking listens to an Australian chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the London borough but is British slang for mad, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Earbash is Australian slang for talking at someone incessantly; to gas is to chatter.

clue.text: One who held up Heaven gets time in the end

blocks.note: the Titan who bore the heavens on his shoulders
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The Titan holding up the sky is finally given some relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean finally, after a long wait, so they are idiomatic synonyms.

clue.text: Four involved in archly contrived gallantry

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it
contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: Four people take part in a coyly staged display of courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is the courteous code of the medieval knight, and gallantry is a synonym.

clue.text: Piece of rabbit that a couple will share?

definitions.text: Piece of rabbit that a couple will share?

blocks.clueFragment: Piece of rabbit that a couple will share?
blocks.note: surface reading: two diners splitting a portion of rabbit meat
setter's reading: rabbit is British slang for talk, so this is a bit of chat between exactly two people

explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is British rhyming slang (rabbit and pork, talk) for chatter, not a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between just two people is called this, a cryptic sense of chat.

clue.text: A shelter for little piggies in Wellington?

definitions.text: A shelter for little piggies in Wellington?

blocks.clueFragment: A shelter for little piggies in Wellington?
blocks.note: surface reading: a pigsty in the New Zealand capital
setter's reading: the little piggies are toes, and a Wellington is a rubber boot

explanation.walkthrough: A Wellington is a rubber boot; 'this little piggy' is the nursery rhyme counted on the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reinforced cover over the front of a boot protects the wearer's feet.

clue.text: Promote Delaware and Maine repeatedly as all the same in Paris

indicators.note: done repeatedly means done more than once, so the same piece appears twice in a row

blocks.note: to tout is to push or advertise
DE is the US state abbreviation
ME, the state abbreviation, given twice

explanation.surface: A marketer pushes two American states as if they were interchangeable.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means nevertheless or even so, matching the English idiom.

clue.text: Musical symbol lent force in new arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement puts the same letters in a different order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical sign gives power to a fresh arrangement of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This C clef placed on the fourth line of the staff is a notation sign in written music.

clue.text: Old head of Orica is brilliant Australian

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, its opening letter

blocks.note: ex means former
first letter of Orica

explanation.surface: A former boss of the mining firm Orica is a brilliant Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: Orica is a big Australian explosives company; brilliant is an adjective here, not praise for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Exo is Australian slang for excellent, a clipped form of the word.

clue.text: Old red line some players must not cross?

definitions.text: line some players must not cross

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for old
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A historic red line that certain players may not step over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old red' wants to be a colour; it is O plus a famous communist.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the mark on the floor behind which a darts player must stand to throw.

clue.text: Star necking bit of temazepam gets surprise

indicators.note: necking means swallowing, so one piece goes down inside the other
a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: the Sun is a star
first letter of temazepam

explanation.surface: A celebrity swallowing sleeping pills causes a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Necking is British slang for gulping down a drink or pill.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or amaze them, a verb synonym for surprise.

clue.text: I used to think of God and naked beaux

indicators.note: naked means stripped of coverings, so the word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: the Norse thunder god
beaux without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone recalls once dreaming of a deity and nude boyfriends.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person by the answer himself, a thinker of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was a 19th-century American philosopher and essayist, so thinking was his trade.

clue.text: Sadly, got AA memo about McLean's end just now

indicators.note: something gone sadly has turned out badly, so the letters fall into disorder
about means surrounding, so the letters wrap around the next piece
a word's end is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
final letter of McLean

explanation.surface: Someone named McLean just received a gloomy note from the Automobile Association.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's motoring breakdown organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean very recently, a few seconds earlier, as idiomatic synonyms.

clue.text: Gangster flash northern detective nuts

blocks.note: Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
a mo is a moment, as in 'in a flash'
N is the abbreviation for northern
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A mobster shows a policeman from the north that he is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' wants to mean mad; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are edible seeds commonly classed as nuts, an example of the category.

clue.text: Sick European brought up boy for novelist

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up makes it read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: ill means sick
E is the abbreviation for European
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An ailing European raises a boy who becomes a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Ellison was the American author of the novel Invisible Man.

clue.text: Icy city spies will infiltrate close to Poyang Lake

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so these pieces go within the others
the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: final letter of Poyang
LA is Los Angeles
the US intelligence agency
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Agents from a city sneak up to China's Poyang Lake in freezing weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Poyang Lake is in China; it reads as one place name but splits into a letter of Poyang plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial means extremely cold, like a glacier, a synonym for icy.

clue.text: Priest shot retired gypsy in organised persecution

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
a shot is a go, an attempt
a Rom is a Romany person

explanation.surface: A cleric shoots a Romany man who has stopped working, as part of a campaign of persecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a gunshot verb but is a noun meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is a violent massacre or persecution of an ethnic group, deliberately organised.

clue.text: Huge firm with a large holding in forfeiture

indicators.note: holding something in means keeping it enclosed within

blocks.note: CO is a company
a forfeiture is a loss
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A massive company holds a large stake that is being forfeited.
explanation.walkthrough: CO plus A and L makes COAL, which holds LOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, like the Colossus of Rhodes, a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Rhodes and other parasites Catholic rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: lice are parasites
C is the abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: Rhodes and other bloodsuckers were turned away by a Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first name of Cecil Rhodes, the imperialist; 'other parasites' suggests he was one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Rhodes was the British colonialist who founded Rhodesia and the Rhodes scholarships.

clue.text: 'Small' Conservative old females mock

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
O is an abbreviation for old
F for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Elderly women ridicule a Conservative described as small.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff at something is to ridicule or jeer at it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dis nurse in charge related to very old Greeks

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and by extension the underworld
EN is an enrolled nurse
IC is short for in charge

explanation.surface: A nurse in charge of a ward describes something linked to ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dis' looks like slang for disrespect but is the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenic means relating to the Greeks, especially of the classical period.

clue.text: Hard to entertain tenor showing no interest

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to host them inside, so one piece takes in another

blocks.note: solid means hard
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A tenor singer is a tough audience who looks bored.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is impassive and unemotional, showing little feeling or curiosity.

clue.text: One that might have a hand in a bungled action

definitions.text: One that might have a hand in

blocks.clueFragment: One that might have a hand in
blocks.note: first meaning: a fur tube for warming the hands
second meaning: a fumbled catch or clumsy failure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a hand in' sounds like being involved; it is literal, a hand put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cylindrical hand-warmer and, as a noun, a clumsy blunder such as a dropped ball.

clue.text: Picture that doesn't say a thousand words?

definitions.text: Picture that doesn't say a thousand words?

blocks.clueFragment: Picture that doesn't say a thousand words?
blocks.note: surface reading: a twist on the proverb that a picture is worth a thousand words
setter's reading: a picture is a movie, and this kind has no spoken dialogue

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb leads you to a still image; 'picture' here means a motion picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Early movies had no recorded sound, so the actors never spoke a word to the audience.
